problem.title: Design a Distributed Web Crawler & Indexing Frontier (Googlebot Scale)
problem.prompt: Design a distributed web crawler indexing 10B web pages/month (~4,000 pages/sec sustained, 10K+ peak) with strict per-host politeness, `robots.txt` compliance, < 2% duplicate content storage, and resilience against infinite-URL crawler traps.

spark.summary: Shard the Mercator URL Frontier by `hash(host)`, pair with async DNS caching, RocksDB/Bloom URL deduplication, 64-bit SimHash content dedup, and URL-depth/pattern trap guards.
spark.keyTakeaway: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, consistent-hash by hostname (not full URL) so each host's politeness timer and `robots.txt` cache live on one shard.
spark.byteSummary:
Crawling 10B pages/month (~4,000 pages/sec) across a distributed fetcher fleet breaks down quickly if URLs are sharded by `hash(url)`—because 50 workers would hit `example.com` simultaneously.

Sharding the Mercator Frontier by `hash(hostname)` guarantees every domain's Back Queue, `robots.txt` cache (24h TTL), and politeness timer reside on a single owner shard. Fetchers use non-blocking async DNS resolvers (avoiding glibc `getaddrinfo` thread blocking) and stream parsed pages through a 64-bit **SimHash** (Hamming distance <= 3) near-duplicate detector before indexing.

To defeat infinite calendar/session-ID crawler traps, enforce max URL length, max path depth, and per-host query-param entropy caps.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Distributed Web Crawler & Indexing Frontier (Googlebot Scale) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, consistent-hash by hostname (not full URL) so each host's politeness timer and `robots.txt` cache live on one shard.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

prerequisites.title: Distributed Web Crawler & Mercator URL Frontier
prerequisites.summary: The Mercator URL Frontier separates crawl priority (Front Queues) from per-host politeness (Back Queues) so high-priority domains are crawled fast without DDoSing any single origin server.

prerequisites.title: Consistent Hashing & Virtual Nodes
prerequisites.summary: Consistent hashing assigns data keys to servers in a way that limits how many keys move when servers are added or removed. This helps avoid widespread cache misses and sudden load on databases.
